EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows typical aliphatic C–H stretches (2940, 2841 cm⁻¹) and strong CH₃/CH₂ deformation bands (1458, 1367 cm⁻¹). A pronounced band near 1158 cm⁻¹ together with a strong symmetric band at 855 cm⁻¹ and additional features at 974/1007 cm⁻¹ are characteristic of aliphatic ether C–O–C stretching modes: open-chain dialkyl ethers display a strong symmetric C–O–C stretch around 850-880 cm⁻¹ and an asymmetric stretch in the 1100-1160 cm⁻¹ region. Candidate 4 (CCOCCC(C)OC) is the only dialkyl diether in the list; it lacks O–H or N–H groups, consistent with the absence of Raman bands near 3200-3400 cm⁻¹. Other candidates either contain nitro, hydroxyl or ring heteroatoms that would introduce additional characteristic bands not observed. Thus the dialkyl ether (candidate 4) best fits the observed Raman peaks.
